title: Keto Vanilla Almond Wedding Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft almond vanilla keto cupcakes with a smooth swirled frosting, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These keto vanilla almond wedding cupcakes taste soft, buttery, and lightly sweet. I made them for a friend's small backyard wedding and everyone asked for the recipe. Almond flour and sour cream keep the crumb moist without any sugar or gluten. The vanilla and almond extract combo gives a bakery style flavor that still feels light. The frosting pipes into a tall smooth swirl, perfect for a wedding table. I tested three batches in my home kitchen before this version held its shape best. This recipe works for bridal showers, anniversaries, or any low carb celebration. It is simple enough for a first time keto baker.
ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese, softened, for frosting
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F and line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, erythritol, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs, melted butter, sour cream, vanilla, and almond extract until smooth.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Add almond milk one tablespoon at a time until the batter is thick but pourable.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean and tops spring back.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully before frosting.
Beat cream cheese and butter together until smooth and light.
Add powdered erythritol and vanilla, then beat 2 more minutes until fluffy.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake using a large star tip.
tips: Cool cupcakes completely before frosting or the swirl will melt and slide.
Use fine almond flour, not almond meal, for a smoother crumb.
If your kitchen is warm, chill the frosting 10 minutes before piping for a cleaner swirl.
Swap almond extract for lemon extract if you want a brighter wedding flavor.

faq.question: Can I make these keto wedding cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the morning of your event for the freshest swirl.

faq.question: Why did my keto cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: Dense cupcakes usually mean overmixed batter or almond meal instead of fine almond flour. Stir just until combined and use finely ground almond flour for a lighter crumb.

faq.question: Can I use a different sweetener in this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes, a monk fruit and erythritol blend works well in both the cake and frosting. Avoid pure erythritol alone in large amounts, since it can taste cool on its own.

faq.question: How do I get a smooth wedding style swirl on keto frosting?
faq.answer: Chill the cream cheese frosting slightly, then pipe with steady pressure and a large star tip. Practice one swirl on a plate first to check the texture before piping the cupcakes.

conclusion: These keto vanilla almond wedding cupcakes bring a soft, elegant option to any low carb celebration. Once you get the swirl technique down, this recipe becomes a easy go to for showers, anniversaries, and small weddings.
